title: Order Desk Rule for Strip Refills: Choosing Between an Old and a New Written Order
content:
A test-strip refill on the Blood Glucose Testing Supply Program ships at the rate of one written order for test strips, and when a newer order is on file the order desk applies the rule below.

The rate is that of the program's newest written order for test strips when it is not the order behind the latest strip refill and was signed within the last 30 days; it is the lower of that newest order's and the earlier order's units per 30 days when the newest order is not the order behind the latest strip refill and was signed more than 30 days ago; and otherwise it is the rate of the order behind the latest strip refill.

The newest written order for test strips is the one with the latest order date. An order signed within the last 30 days has an order date 30 days or fewer before today; at 31 days or more it was signed more than 30 days ago. The rate so read is the rate the refill ships at.

Boundary pairs (hypothetical orders; the latest strip refill rests on an order for 5 units per 30 days):

- A newer order for 8 units dated 30 days ago: the rate is 8. The same order dated 31 days ago: the rate is 5, the lower of 8 and 5.
- A newer order for 2 units dated 31 days ago: the rate is 2, the lower of 2 and 5. The same order dated 10 days ago: the rate is 2.
- No order newer than the one behind the refill, or the newest order is that same order: the rate is 5.
